description: Places notes against the bars, chord changes and cadences of the chart on the cable, in breath groups with pauses between them. Patch it to an mpxVoice for a melody, or to fromMPX for the rhythm alone

params.text: The division the notes fall on, and so the shortest note that can happen: a quarter, an eighth, a sixteenth or an eighth triplet. A fine setting permits short notes rather than forcing them
How long a breath group is, in seconds. Real phrases hold their length in seconds and take more beats as the tempo rises
How much the groups differ in length from one another. At nought they are all the same length; high makes some short and some long, and fragments them toward the end of a phrase
Where a group starts: left mostly a pickup before the beat, centre the mix in pop songs, right mostly after the beat. A phrase's pickup can lead in from the bar before
Where a group ends: left mostly off the beat, right mostly on a strong beat
The silence at the end of each breath group, in half beats up to 2, so the phrase is heard in parts rather than as one run
The silence at the end of a phrase, in half beats up to a bar of 4
How long a group's last note is held: about one beat at left, two at right. Past the middle it also rings on into the pause
How often a whole phrase is dropped, with nothing played from its beginning to its end — the longest silence this module makes
How many of the grid slots sound, from a few notes in a group to nearly every slot
How far the notes move off the strong slots onto the weak ones between them, so the line pushes against the beat instead of sitting on it
How far the rhythm follows the chords: notes on the changes and held there, some changes anticipated, more notes over quick chords
Note lengths, from short and separated to long enough to run into the next note
How far the loudness moves: across each phrase by LOUDNESS SHAPE, from phrase to phrase, and onto held notes and anticipations. At nought every note is alike
How far every choice may depart from its likeliest outcome. At nought the seed makes no difference
The pitch the notes are sent at, for hearing the rhythm without a melody. An mpxVoice downstream replaces it with a note of its own
The number every choice here is drawn from, added to the chart's own seed. Change it for a different line from the same settings; put it back for the line you had
Pressed, the seed above is used on its own and the chart's is ignored, so this line stays as it is while the rest of the patch follows the chart
How closely a phrase restates the one before it. At nought each is fresh; at one every onset comes back except in its last group, which is always decided afresh so the phrase ends in its own place
How many phrases pass before the whole sequence of variations returns. At four, the fifth phrase is the first one again; at one, every phrase is alike
How much a returning section plays what it played the first time. The chart says which section a phrase is in and which time round this is
How often a closing cadence's arrival is also the next phrase's first note, with no breath between them. At nought every phrase breathes
Records every phrase and note it sends, and every change of setting, to a file in the DreamerMPX folder of your Rack user folder. In the right-click menu
How often a beat sounds the middle unit of the triplet — the one a swung pair skips — as a share of the beats played. Real jazz solos do it on about eight per cent of them
The loudness across a phrase: left falls from its start, as jazz solos do; right rises to a peak and falls, as a sung phrase does. The last note is softer either way
How often a breath group restates the rhythm of one of the three groups before it, then carries on in its own way. Pop songs do it about a third of the time

inputs.text: Takes the chart, which supplies the beat, the metre, the chord changes, the cadences and the phrase boundaries
Adds to the density knob, 0 to 10V across its full range, so the line can thicken and thin while it plays

outputs.text: Carries the notes as an MPX stream, with a level and a duration on each

notes: there is no clock input. Every note is placed by the beat the chart publishes, so this stops, rewinds and loops exactly when the chart does
presets Pop 1 to 3 and Jazz 1 to 3, a ballad to up-tempo, are in the right-click menu, with mpxVoice presets of the same names to go with them
a restated figure is marked on the cable, so a melody voice with MOTIF turned up brings back its pitches as well as its rhythm
the tempo is measured from how fast the chart's beat advances, since the cable carries the beat but not the tempo
a phrase is decided whole when it begins. A control moved part-way through takes effect at the start of the next group rather than at once
without a chart patched in there is no beat and no metre, so nothing is played and neither lamp flashes
